q: A company's board of directors includes a majority of independent members who meet regularly without management to oversee financial reporting, and the company enforces a written code of conduct. Under the COSO 2013 Internal Control-Integrated Framework, these practices relate most directly to which component?
choices: Control environment
Monitoring activities
Control activities
Risk assessment
exp: COSO's control environment principles include commitment to integrity and ethical values and board independence and oversight of internal control. Monitoring is about evaluating whether components are functioning, not about board structure itself.

q: When identifying risks to its financial reporting objectives, management of a public company specifically evaluates incentives and pressures, opportunities, and attitudes that could lead to fraudulent reporting. Under COSO 2013, this activity is part of which component?
choices: Control environment
Information and communication
Risk assessment
Control activities
exp: COSO's risk assessment component includes Principle 8, which requires the organization to consider the potential for fraud when assessing risks to achieving objectives. The control environment sets the tone but is not where fraud risks are identified and analyzed.

q: A company's internal audit department periodically evaluates whether key controls over revenue are operating as designed and reports deficiencies to the audit committee and senior management. Under COSO 2013, this function is part of which component?
choices: Control activities
Monitoring activities
Risk assessment
Information and communication
exp: Separate evaluations, such as internal audit reviews, and the communication of deficiencies to those responsible for corrective action are monitoring activities (COSO Principles 16 and 17). The controls being tested are control activities, but evaluating them is monitoring.

q: A company maintains an anonymous whistleblower hotline that lets employees report suspected improprieties directly to the audit committee, bypassing normal reporting lines. Under COSO 2013, the hotline is most directly an element of which component?
choices: Control activities
Risk assessment
Monitoring activities
Information and communication
exp: COSO Principle 14 (internal communication) specifically mentions separate communication lines, such as whistleblower hotlines, as a way to allow anonymous or confidential communication when normal channels are ineffective. Many candidates choose control environment or monitoring, but COSO places it under information and communication.

q: A company restricts access to its production programs and data so that only authorized IT personnel can make changes. Under COSO 2013, this type of control is classified within which component?
choices: Control environment
Monitoring activities
Risk assessment
Control activities
exp: COSO Principle 11 requires the organization to select and develop general control activities over technology, which include security and access controls. These are control activities, even though they relate to the IT environment.

q: Under the COSO 2013 framework, an effective system of internal control requires that
choices: no deficiencies of any kind exist in any component
each of the five components and relevant principles is present and functioning, and the components operate together in an integrated manner
the organization has an internal audit function that reports directly to the board
all 17 principles are documented in written policies approved by the board
exp: COSO requires each component and relevant principle to be present and functioning, and the five components to operate together, with no major deficiency. Minor deficiencies may exist in an effective system, and COSO does not require an internal audit function or written documentation of every principle.

q: A receiving clerk and an accounts payable clerk agree to process invoices from a fictitious vendor, with the receiving clerk preparing false receiving reports. The company's three-way match control did not detect the scheme. This illustrates which inherent limitation of internal control?
choices: Collusion among two or more individuals
Management override of controls
Human error in applying a control
Cost-benefit constraints on control design
exp: Segregation of duties and matching controls can be circumvented when people in incompatible roles collude, which is an inherent limitation recognized by COSO and AU-C 315. Management override involves managers, not clerks, bypassing controls.

q: Which of the following pairs of duties, if performed by the same employee, represents the most serious weakness in segregation of duties?
choices: Preparing a remittance list and restrictively endorsing incoming checks
Preparing the bank deposit and taking it to the bank
Receiving customer payments and posting them to the accounts receivable subsidiary ledger
Maintaining the general ledger and preparing the trial balance
exp: Combining custody of cash receipts with recording in customer accounts lets an employee steal receipts and conceal the theft, for example through lapping. The other pairs combine duties of the same type, either custody with custody or recording with recording.

q: During a nonissuer audit, the auditor determines that a control deficiency creates a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the financial statements will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. Under AU-C 265, this deficiency is
choices: a significant deficiency
a control deficiency that need only be communicated orally
a material weakness
a deficiency in design but not in operation
exp: AU-C 265 defines a material weakness as a deficiency, or combination of deficiencies, with a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A significant deficiency is less severe but still merits the attention of those charged with governance.

q: Under AU-C 265, how and when must the auditor of a nonissuer communicate significant deficiencies and material weaknesses identified during the audit?
choices: Orally to management, before the end of fieldwork
In writing to management only, within 30 days after the report date
In the auditor's report on the financial statements, as an other-matter paragraph
In writing to management and those charged with governance, no later than 60 days following the report release date
exp: AU-C 265 requires written communication of significant deficiencies and material weaknesses to management and those charged with governance, preferably by the report release date and no later than 60 days after it. Oral communication is not enough for these deficiencies, and they are not reported in the opinion.

q: During a nonissuer audit, the auditor identifies several control deficiencies that are neither significant deficiencies nor material weaknesses but are important enough to merit management's attention. Under AU-C 265, the auditor should
choices: communicate them to management on a timely basis, either in writing or orally
communicate them in writing to those charged with governance within 60 days
not communicate them, because only significant deficiencies and material weaknesses require communication
include them in the management representation letter
exp: AU-C 265 requires the auditor to communicate other deficiencies that merit management's attention to management on a timely basis, and oral communication is allowed. The written communication requirement applies only to significant deficiencies and material weaknesses.

q: An auditor finds that the review of journal entries over $50,000 was not performed for three months. No misstatements were found in those entries. Under AU-C 265, how does the absence of an actual misstatement affect the evaluation of the deficiency's severity?
choices: The deficiency cannot be more than a minor deficiency, because no misstatement occurred

Severity depends on whether there is a reasonable possibility that the control could fail to prevent or detect a misstatement and on the potential magnitude, not on whether a misstatement actually occurred
The deficiency must be classified as a material weakness, because the control was not performed
The deficiency need not be evaluated, because substantive procedures found no errors
exp: AU-C 265 states that the severity of a deficiency does not depend on whether a misstatement actually occurred. It depends on the likelihood and potential magnitude of misstatement. An absence of errors in substantive testing does not show that the control is effective.

q: When evaluating the severity of a control deficiency, the auditor identifies a compensating control. Which statement is correct?
choices: A compensating control eliminates the deficiency, so it need not be considered further

A compensating control may limit the severity of the deficiency if it operates at a level of precision that would prevent, or detect and correct, a material misstatement, but it does not eliminate the deficiency
Compensating controls are considered only in audits of issuers
Compensating controls increase the severity of the deficiency because they show that controls are redundant
exp: Under AU-C 265 and AS 2201, effective compensating controls can reduce the severity of a deficiency, for example from a material weakness to a significant deficiency, but the deficiency still exists. To be effective, the compensating control must operate with sufficient precision.

q: Which of the following is an indicator of a material weakness in internal control?
choices: The auditor identifies a material misstatement in the current-period financial statements that the entity's controls would not have detected
Internal audit identifies an immaterial error and management corrects it on a timely basis
The company converts to a new general ledger system during the year
The auditor proposes no audit adjustments for the year
exp: AU-C 265 and AS 2201 list indicators of a material weakness: an auditor-identified material misstatement not detected by the entity's controls, fraud by senior management, a restatement to correct a material misstatement, and ineffective audit committee oversight. An immaterial error that internal controls caught is evidence that controls are working.

q: In an integrated audit under PCAOB AS 2201, the auditor uses a top-down approach to select controls to test. This approach begins with
choices: testing the operating effectiveness of each transaction-level control in the significant processes

the financial statement level and the auditor's understanding of overall risks to internal control over financial reporting, then entity-level controls, then significant accounts and relevant assertions
the controls that management has identified as most costly to operate
the IT general controls over every application in the company
exp: AS 2201 describes a top-down approach that starts at the financial statement level, considers entity-level controls, and then moves to significant accounts, disclosures, and relevant assertions. Only then does the auditor select transaction-level controls. Starting with every transaction-level control is the bottom-up approach the standard moves away from.

q: In an integrated audit of an issuer with a December 31 year-end, the auditor identifies a material weakness that existed at December 31. Management fully remediates the weakness in February, before the auditor's report is issued, and the auditor confirms the remediated control is working. Under PCAOB AS 2201, the auditor's opinion on internal control over financial reporting should be
choices: unmodified, because the weakness was remediated before the report date
qualified, with a paragraph describing the remediation
a disclaimer, because the remediation creates a scope limitation
adverse, because the material weakness existed as of December 31
exp: The ICFR opinion is as of the assessment date, December 31. A material weakness that existed at that date requires an adverse opinion even if it is remediated afterward. AS 2201 does not permit a qualified opinion because of a material weakness.

q: In an integrated audit, the auditor identifies an entity-level control in which management reviews detailed monthly results by product line and investigates differences from expectations. If this control monitors other controls and operates at a level of precision that would adequately prevent or detect material misstatements, the auditor may
choices: eliminate all testing of controls in the related processes and all substantive procedures
conclude that no walkthroughs are needed for any process
not consider the control, because entity-level controls are relevant only to the control environment
reduce the testing of other controls related to the relevant assertions
exp: AS 2201 notes that precise entity-level controls can sufficiently address the risk for an assertion, which allows the auditor to reduce testing of other controls. Substantive procedures for material accounts are always required, so eliminating them would be wrong.

q: In obtaining an understanding of internal control in a financial statement audit, the auditor wants to determine whether a control over credit approval has been implemented. Under AU-C 315, which approach is appropriate?
choices: Inquiry of the credit manager alone is sufficient
Rely on the prior-year conclusion if the control was implemented last year
Perform procedures in addition to inquiry, such as observing the control or inspecting documents showing its application
Obtain a written representation from management that the control exists
exp: AU-C 315 states that inquiry alone is not sufficient to evaluate design and determine implementation. The auditor combines inquiry with observation, inspection, or a walkthrough. Management representations do not replace that evidence.

q: Under AU-C 315, as amended by SAS No. 145, which of the following controls must the auditor identify and evaluate for design and implementation, even if the auditor does not plan to test its operating effectiveness?
choices: Controls over the efficiency of production scheduling
Controls over journal entries, including nonstandard journal entries
All controls in every business process
Controls that management considers least important
exp: SAS No. 145 requires the auditor to identify controls over journal entries, controls that address significant risks, controls the auditor plans to test, and others in its judgment, and to evaluate their design and implementation. Operational efficiency controls are generally not relevant, and not all controls in every process must be identified.

q: Which of the following is an IT general control rather than an application control?
choices: Requiring that program changes be approved, tested, and authorized before being moved into production
An edit check that rejects sales orders exceeding a customer's credit limit
A matching routine that compares purchase orders, receiving reports, and invoices
A limit test that flags payroll hours over 60 in a week
exp: General IT controls over program changes, access, and IT operations support the continued effective functioning of application controls. Edit checks, three-way matching, and limit tests are application controls embedded in specific transaction processing.

q: Before a batch of payroll time records is processed, the computer totals the employee identification numbers in the batch and compares the result with a total computed manually when the batch was prepared. This control is primarily designed to detect
choices: employees paid at an incorrect wage rate
hours worked that exceed a reasonable limit
missing, added, or altered records in the batch
payroll charged to the wrong department
exp: A hash total is a sum of a field with no meaning in itself, such as ID numbers, and it changes if records are lost, added, or altered between preparation and processing. Wage rates and hour limits are addressed by validity checks and limit tests.

q: Which of the following is a detective control rather than a preventive control?
choices: A monthly bank reconciliation prepared by an employee independent of cash handling and recording
Requiring two authorized signatures on checks over $10,000
Requiring credit approval before goods are shipped to customers
Using passwords to restrict access to the vendor master file
exp: A bank reconciliation identifies errors or irregularities after they have occurred, which makes it a detective control. Dual signatures, credit approval, and access restrictions operate before a transaction is completed to prevent misstatements.

q: A small nonissuer has only two accounting employees, so complete segregation of duties is not practical. Which of the following is most likely to mitigate the risk created by the lack of segregation?
choices: Rotating the two employees' duties every month
Having the external auditor perform the bank reconciliations
Increasing the number of journal entries recorded each month
Active involvement of the owner-manager in approving disbursements and reviewing bank statements and reconciliations
exp: AU-C 315 recognizes that in smaller entities, an owner-manager's direct involvement can compensate for limited segregation of duties, although it increases the risk of management override. The external auditor performing client controls would impair independence and is not an entity control.

q: Which controls are generally relevant to a financial statement audit?
choices: Only controls over the efficiency and effectiveness of operations
Primarily controls related to financial reporting objectives, although some operations or compliance controls may be relevant if they relate to data the auditor uses
All controls in the entity, regardless of objective
Only controls over compliance with laws and regulations
exp: COSO's objectives are operations, reporting, and compliance. Controls related to financial reporting are generally relevant to an audit. Operations and compliance controls are relevant only when they affect data the auditor evaluates or uses in procedures, for example production statistics used in analytics.

q: Under COSO's Enterprise Risk Management-Integrating with Strategy and Performance (2017), defining the organization's risk appetite belongs to which component?
choices: Strategy and Objective-Setting
Governance and Culture
Review and Revision
Information, Communication, and Reporting
exp: The 2017 COSO ERM framework places defining risk appetite under Strategy and Objective-Setting, alongside analyzing business context and formulating business objectives. Governance and Culture covers board oversight, operating structures, and core values instead.

q: At the end of a nonissuer audit, the auditor identified no material weaknesses and no significant deficiencies. Management asks for a letter stating that no significant deficiencies were identified. Under AU-C 265, the auditor
choices: may issue the letter if it is restricted to management's use
should not issue a written communication stating that no significant deficiencies were identified
must issue the letter to those charged with governance
may issue the letter only if the auditor tested all controls
exp: AU-C 265 prohibits a written communication stating that no significant deficiencies were identified, because users could misunderstand the limited assurance involved. A communication stating that no material weaknesses were identified is permitted, which is why the request for a no-significant-deficiency letter is a trap.

q: In an integrated audit under PCAOB AS 2201, as the risk associated with a control increases, the auditor's use of the work of internal auditors and others to test that control should
choices: increase, because more evidence is needed
remain the same, because the work of others is evaluated only on competence
decrease, with the auditor performing more of the work
be eliminated only for controls that operate monthly
exp: AS 2201 states that as the risk associated with a control increases, the auditor should rely less on the work of others and perform more of the work personally. Competence and objectivity of the others also matter, but risk is a separate factor that limits use.

q: An auditor wants to document its understanding of the sales and cash receipts process in a form that clearly shows the flow of documents, the processing steps, and the separation of duties among departments. Which form of documentation is best suited to this purpose?
choices: An internal control questionnaire with yes or no answers
A narrative memorandum
A listing of all controls tested in the prior year
A systems flowchart
exp: A flowchart shows the sequence of documents and processing across departments, which makes gaps in segregation of duties and missing controls easier to see. Questionnaires are efficient for spotting missing controls but do not show the flow of transactions.

q: In a financial statement audit of a nonissuer, what is the auditor's responsibility for identifying deficiencies in internal control?
choices: The auditor must communicate deficiencies identified during the audit but is not required to perform procedures designed to identify all deficiencies
The auditor must perform procedures sufficient to express an opinion on internal control
The auditor must test every control relevant to financial reporting to identify all deficiencies
The auditor has no responsibility regarding control deficiencies
exp: In a financial statement audit, the auditor considers internal control to design audit procedures, not to opine on it. AU-C 265 requires communication of deficiencies that come to the auditor's attention, but not a search for all deficiencies. An ICFR opinion requires a separate examination or an integrated audit.

q: In an integrated audit, the auditor performs a walkthrough of the purchasing process. Under PCAOB AS 2201, which is a primary objective of a walkthrough?
choices: To provide sufficient evidence of operating effectiveness for the entire year
To replace substantive tests of accounts payable
To understand the flow of transactions, verify the points at which misstatements could occur, and evaluate the design and implementation of controls
To select a statistical sample of purchase transactions for testing
exp: AS 2201 describes walkthroughs, which follow a transaction from origination through processing and recording, as a way to achieve objectives such as understanding the flow of transactions, identifying where misstatements could occur, and evaluating control design. A single walkthrough does not establish operating effectiveness over the period.
